title: End-to-end streaming flow-control postmortem and capacity hardening plan
creator: Jordan Lee
description: This ticket captures the postmortem analysis and tracking actions after a cross-region streaming outage that produced client disconnects, truncated token streams, and high rates of reconnects during a capacity spike. The goal is to remediate short-term fallout, harden autoscaling and flow-control, and reduce the probability of recurrence by adding instrumentation, fallbacks, and client/server protocol fixes.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-28 22:04 UTC a sudden traffic spike combined with a recent batching heuristic change caused sustained head-of-line blocking on serving workers. Clients experienced partial token streams (unexpected stream termination), connection resets, and long tail latencies. The issue affected hosted API customers in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for ~46 minutes; retries amplified pressure and delayed recovery.
timeline: 2026-02-28 21:58 UTC - anomalous traffic ramp begins (small spike from a customer load test).
2026-02-28 22:04 UTC - first alerts: elevated socket resets and stream errors in the streaming router.
2026-02-28 22:07 UTC - on-call paged; initial mitigation: route small-per-request traffic to cold path.
2026-02-28 22:10 UTC - autoscaler did not add capacity due to metric threshold mismatch (metric used: successful_requests_per_minute, which dropped as streams stalled).
2026-02-28 22:18 UTC - partial rollout of a temporary token-batching cap to reduce head-of-line blocking.
2026-02-28 22:50 UTC - traffic stabilized after manual router throttling and connection backpressure adjustments.
2026-02-28 23:00 UTC - incident declared mitigated. Post-incident analysis started next day.
observed_behavior: Multiple clients received 'stream closed' after an incomplete token sequence (last token cut mid-word).
Server-side logs showed worker tasks stuck in 'awaiting cache lock' while other tasks queued large batched sends.
Socket-level resets (RST) spiked on the streaming gateway due to buffer exhaustion and timeouts, not immediate kernel-level drops.
Autoscaler failed to trigger because the primary scale metric decreased (requests/s) while backlog and queue_depth increased.
Retry storms from client SDKs worsened the overload; retry/backoff heuristics didn't account for streaming partial failures.
root_cause: Regression from batching heuristic: an aggressive batch-aggregation change increased max batch wait to 120ms for high-concurrency traffic, causing larger batches and longer head-of-line delays under bursty arrivals.
KV cache lock contention: long-running generation tasks held the cache lock while new streaming requests waited, amplifying token production latency for queued requests.
Metrics mismatch in autoscaler: we relied on successful RPS which collapsed during stalls; we did not expose queue_depth or active_stream_count as primary scaling signals.
Insufficient ingress buffering and gateway tuning: proxy buffer sizes and application-level timeouts allowed backpressure to manifest as socket resets instead of graceful flow-control signals.
Client SDKs lacked clear guidance and non-amplifying retry defaults for streaming errors (immediate retries on partial tokens).
mitigations_taken: Rolled back the aggressive batch-aggregation change to previous stable heuristic within 10 minutes of detection.
Applied a temporary cap on max batch size and reduced max-wait to 40ms for streaming endpoints in impacted regions.
Adjusted gateway socket/buffer timeouts and increased ingress buffer pool by 30% to reduce RSTs during transient pressure.
Implemented a short-term router-level circuit-breaker to reject new long-poll streams when queue_depth > threshold to prevent meltdown.
Notified major customers and recommended client SDK upgrade with exponential backoff for streaming errors.
action_items: Add queue_depth and active_stream_count to autoscaler primary metrics and create a composite scaling rule (owner: infra-autoscale, due: 2026-03-18).
Instrument per-request timeline tracing for streaming pipelines (receive->batch->kv-cache->generate->stream), surface percentiles in Console (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-24).
Introduce fine-grained KV cache locks or lock-free reads for prefix checks to eliminate long lock holds (owner: runtime-team, due: 2026-04-05).
Rework batching heuristic to be latency-aware under bursty arrival patterns; add dynamic 'burst mode' that lowers max-wait when arrival variance spikes (owner: runtime-team, due: 2026-03-29).
Implement server-side stream resume tokens and idempotent chunk replay to allow clients to recover partial-token failures without full restart (owner: api-team, due: 2026-05-10).
Publish a client SDK streaming best-practices doc and set default retry to jittered exponential backoff for partial-token/closed-stream errors (owner: developer-experience, due: 2026-03-15).
Tune gateway TCP and proxy buffers, and add backpressure signalling between gateway and router (owner: networking, due: 2026-03-12 - completed short-term; long-term by 2026-04-01).
Create a chaos test that simulates bursty ingress + slow KV cache to validate fallback behaviors during CI (owner: reliability, due: 2026-04-12).
Add streaming-specific SLA playbook to runbooks with decision tree for when to fail fast vs. accept degraded throughput (owner: support-sre, due: 2026-03-20).
followups: Validate autoscaler metric change in a canary region (us-east-1) for two weeks and monitor false-scaling alerts.
Roll out client SDK update and monitor dropped-stream rate; coordinate with top 10 customers for staged upgrade.
Schedule a cross-team retro to review change gating for batching heuristics and add a pre-deploy smoke test that simulates short bursts.
Track post-deploy error budget consumption for streaming endpoints for 30 days after fixes are complete.
notes: This incident exposed coupling between batching, KV cache locking, autoscaling signals, and client retry behavior. Prioritization favors short-term operational fixes (autoscaler metrics + gateway tuning) while designing longer-term architectural changes (lock-free cache reads, replay tokens).
